body:
Founder real-time, actually dropping a real large file onto the
PARENA editor: "it crashed... if we try to open a too large file it
just chokes".

Root cause, confirmed live: raw_read_all_impl (read-string's own real
host primitive, called by the editor's own load_from_file) grew its
buffer in FIXED 4096-byte steps -- reallocating and copying the
ENTIRE buffer so far on every single grow (a bump arena, nothing ever
freed). Real O(N^2) copy work and real O(N^2) wasted memory for an
N-byte file. Confirmed live: the pre-fix version couldn't even finish
reading a real ~10MB file in 30 real seconds (timed out); a 100+MB
file would exhaust available memory outright.

Fixed with fstat(2)-sized single allocation (the only real caller,
read-string, is documented FileHandle-only) + real doubling growth as
the fallback for when the size hint is wrong. Verified live: the
fixed version reads a real 133.5MB file in 0.526 seconds; the same
~10MB file the old version couldn't finish in 30 seconds now reads in
0.045 seconds.

New real regression test in tests/test_editor_io.c (a real ~8MB file,
asserts read-string completes in well under 2 real seconds -- a real
wall-clock proof, not just "does it crash"). Full local suite (336
tests) + all 5 selfhost domains + test-editor-io clean, zero
regressions. CI green on all 4 jobs (real Windows/macOS included,
confirming the fstat/sys-stat.h portability was fine).

Real, honest scope: this fixes the actual crash/choke -- loading is
now fast and bounded, not accidentally quadratic -- but the whole file
still ends up resident in memory at once. True streaming/windowing
(only the visible portion of a truly huge, GB-scale file ever in
memory) is a real, separate, much larger editor-architecture question,
not attempted here.

PARENA commit 54652f2. CI run 33116118774: all 4 jobs green.

title: Fixed real O(n^2) crash/choke on large files -- raw_read_all_impl grew in fixed 4096-byte steps
